les: Vier dinge wat eers moes bestaan
kaps_punt: Kort oorsig van ontdekkings wat hierdie operasie moontlik gemaak het: narkose; vermyding van infeksie, bloedoortappings, X-strale

items.bewering: 'n Hartoorplanting sit 'n nuwe hart in 'n mens se bors.
items.bron: British Heart Foundation, 'Heart transplant' (bhf.org.uk/informationsupport/treatments/heart-transplant): the failing heart is replaced with a donor heart. 'Nuwe' here means a donor heart, which the begrip entry makes explicit.

items.bewering: Baie ander ontdekkings moes eers daar wees voordat dit kon gebeur. Vier van hulle doen elkeen 'n ander werk vir die operasie.
items.bron: BHF heart transplant page (general anaesthetic, heart-lung bypass machine, lifelong anti-rejection medicine); Britannica and Wikipedia on Christiaan Barnard / Louis Washkansky (the 1967 operation relied on matched blood type and immunosuppression). Each of the four discoveries does a distinct job as described in the blocks below.

items.bewering: Al vier is oor baie jare in verskillende lande ontdek, en elkeen was gereed voordat 'n hart van een mens na 'n ander oorgeplant kon word.
items.bron: Ether anaesthesia: Boston, USA, 1846 (Wikipedia 'Ether Dome', Britannica on Morton). Antisepsis: Lister, Glasgow, 1860s (Museum of Health Care Kingston, 'Sir Joseph Lister'). X-rays: Röntgen, Würzburg, Germany, 1895 (The Scientist, 'The First X-ray, 1895'). Blood groups: Landsteiner, Vienna, 1901 (Stanford Blood Center, 'A Brief History of Blood Transfusion'). All long before the first human heart transplant, Cape Town, 3 December 1967 (Britannica, Christiaan Barnard). Spread of about 55 years, four countries.

items.bewering: Voor narkose was 'n mens wakker en het hy die sny gevoel. 'n Operasie moes toe kort en vinnig wees.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ether Dome' and Britannica on W.T.G. Morton: before 1846 patients were operated on conscious, 'the screaming, struggling patient held down by assistants'; speed was the surgeon's main defence against pain and shock.

items.bewering: Narkose is wanneer medisyne 'n mens laat slaap en niks laat voel nie.
items.bron: NHS (Guy's and St Thomas', Moorfields, NHS 111 Wales): general anaesthesia is 'a state of controlled unconsciousness during which you feel nothing', given by drugs through a vein or as gas; NHS patient material itself calls this being 'asleep'. 'Slaap' is the standard patient-facing simplification and not false at this level; Afrikaans 'narkose' denotes general (not local) anaesthesia.

items.bewering: 'n Hartoorplanting duur ure lank, en die pasiënt moet stil en sonder pyn slaap. Sonder narkose kan 'n dokter nie ure lank in die bors werk nie.
items.bron: BHF heart transplant page: 'Surgery usually takes about 4 to 6 hours', under general anaesthetic.

items.bewering: Baie mense het vroeër 'n operasie oorleef en toe aan die wond gesterf.
items.bron: Museum of Health Care at Kingston, 'Sir Joseph Lister' and EBSCO Research Starters, 'Joseph Lister Performs First Antiseptic Surgical Operation': before antisepsis post-operative wound infection killed a large share of surgical patients (ward mortality from such infection fell to about 15% under Lister's method; earlier amputation figures of roughly 40-45% are cited). 'Baie' is supported; no number is claimed.

items.bewering: Later het mense verstaan dat kieme in 'n wond infeksie veroorsaak. Hande, instrumente, die kamer en die wond is skoongemaak om die kieme dood te maak.
items.bron: Museum of Health Care Kingston and Pfizer/Breakthroughs 'Flashback: Carbolic Acid Sprayer': Lister, building on germ theory, used carbolic acid on instruments, surgeons' hands, wounds and dressings, and sprayed it in the operating theatre air; later aseptic practice cleaned the theatre itself. Each of the four items is supported.

items.bewering: Terwyl die bors ure lank oop is, kan kieme by die wond kom. Sonder skoon werk kan die nuwe hart in 'n liggaam klop wat aan infeksie sterf.
items.bron: BHF (4-6 hour open-chest operation); Britannica and Wikipedia 'Louis Washkansky': the first transplant patient died of pneumonia after 18 days with the new heart working, infection being the main threat to transplant patients. The sentence is phrased as possibility ('kan'), which the sources support.

items.bewering: By 'n bloedoortapping kry 'n pasiënt bloed van 'n ander mens. Dit het in die begin dikwels misluk.
items.bron: Stanford Blood Center, 'A Brief History of Blood Transfusion Through The Years', and AABB 'Highlights of Transfusion Medicine History': before 1901 outcomes were 'essentially luck'; many patients received incompatible blood and died, and blood often clotted during the procedure.

items.bewering: Later het mense ontdek dat daar meer as een bloedgroep is. Die bloed wat inloop, moet by die pasiënt se eie bloed pas. Daarna kon dit veilig gebeur, en later kon bloed gestoor word.
items.bron: Stanford Blood Center and AABB timeline: Landsteiner described ABO groups in 1901; matching by typing first reported by Ottenberg in 1907; citrate anticoagulation (Hustin 1914, Lewisohn 1915) and citrate-glucose storage (Rous and Turner 1916) came afterwards. The sequence groups -> matching -> storage is correct. 'Daarna' does not claim 'immediately', and the lesson does not claim blood groups were the only cause of failure, so the omission of clotting is incomplete rather than false.

items.bewering: By 'n operasie aan die hart verloor 'n mens baie bloed. Nuwe bloed loop in terwyl die dokter nog werk.
items.bron: Wits (WIReDSpace) audit of intraoperative blood product use in cardiac surgery on cardiopulmonary bypass: 90.2% of patients received donor blood products during the operation; Dutch multicentre benchmark (Netherlands Heart Journal, Springer s12471-016-0936-1): cardiac surgery transfusion rates 43-88% by procedure. Supports both the blood loss and transfusion during the operation.

items.bewering: Vroeër kon 'n dokter die hart se vorm en grootte net van buite af skat.
items.bron: Rutgers RWJMS 'History of Cardiac Physical Diagnosis' and PMC5255174 ('Posture in Percussion of the Heart', 1898): before X-rays, heart size and outline were estimated by percussion of the area of cardiac dullness on the chest wall (Auenbrugger 1761, Corvisart, Piorry); PMC3221199 review notes the skill was largely displaced by X-ray and echocardiography.

items.bewering: X-strale maak 'n prent van die binnekant van 'n lewende mens sonder om te sny. Met so 'n prent kon 'n dokter die vorm en grootte van die hart en die longe sien voordat hy sny.
items.bron: The Scientist, 'The First X-ray, 1895' (Röntgen imaged his wife's living hand); PMC5270120 ('Recent Progress in Radiography'): Francis Henry Williams used X-rays to estimate heart size from 1896, the first application of X-rays to cardiology, and X-rays revealed chest structures percussion could not.

items.bewering: 'n Hartoorplanting het ook 'n masjien nodig gehad wat die bloed rondpomp terwyl die hart weg is.
items.blok: Dit is nie die hele lys nie
items.bron: BHF heart transplant page: 'You'll be connected to a heart-lung bypass machine to keep blood pumping around your body during surgery.' The machine also oxygenates the blood, which the lesson does not mention; omission, not error.

items.bewering: Medisyne moes ook keer dat die liggaam die nuwe hart afwys.
items.blok: Dit is nie die hele lys nie
items.bron: BHF heart transplant page (immunosuppressant medicines taken for life to prevent rejection); Britannica, Christiaan Barnard / Washkansky (drugs suppressed immunity so the body would not reject the heart).

items.bewering: narkose: Wanneer medisyne 'n pasiënt laat slaap en niks laat voel nie.
items.bron: NHS general anaesthesia pages (controlled unconsciousness induced by drugs, during which the patient feels nothing). Consistent with the study block wording.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak. 'n Enkele kiem is te klein om met die blote oog te sien.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster Medical, 'germ': a microorganism, especially a pathogenic agent such as a bacterium or virus; Dictionary.com, 'germ'. The singular framing ('n enkele kiem') correctly avoids the case of visible mould colonies. Whether viruses are 'living' is debated at the margin, but standard reference definitions treat germs as microorganisms and the entry says 'kan', not that every germ causes illness.

items.bewering: infeksie: Wanneer kieme in die liggaam groei en die liggaam siek kan maak.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster Medical sense of infection as invasion and multiplication of pathogenic microorganisms in the body; 'kan' correctly allows for infection without illness.

items.bewering: bloedoortapping: Wanneer 'n pasiënt bloed van 'n ander mens kry.
items.bron: Stanford Blood Center, history of blood transfusion (transfer of blood from a donor to a recipient).

items.bewering: bloedgroep: Een van die soorte bloed wat mense het.
items.bron: Stanford Blood Center / AABB: ABO groups are the types into which human blood is classified (Landsteiner 1901). Simple but accurate; does not claim only humans have blood groups.

items.bewering: X-strale: Strale wat 'n prent van die binnekant van 'n lewende liggaam maak.
items.bron: The Scientist, 'The First X-ray, 1895'; PMC5270120. A definition by medical use: true as stated. X-rays also image non-living objects, but the entry does not say they only work on living bodies.

items.bewering: hartoorplanting: 'n Operasie wat 'n siek hart met 'n ander hart vervang, gewoonlik die hart van 'n mens wat gesterf het.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Louis Washkansky' and Britannica, Christiaan Barnard: donor Denise Darvall, whose brain death had been confirmed; BHF heart transplant page (donor heart via organ donation). 'Gewoonlik' properly covers rare exceptions (e.g. domino transplants).

items.bewering: instrumente: Die gereedskap waarmee 'n dokter tydens 'n operasie werk.
items.bron: Standard meaning of surgical instruments; consistent with Lister sources (Museum of Health Care Kingston) on disinfecting instruments.

opsomming: Every checkable claim held up against sources, and nothing needs changing. The lesson has no superlatives (no 'first', 'oldest' or 'only'). Its one figurative image, an X-ray as a 'picture of the inside', maps correctly. The two simplifications a person might question are fine at this level: anaesthesia as 'sleep' is how the NHS words it for patients, and the blood-transfusion block leaves out clotting without saying anything false.
